correctness.rationale: Reconstructed P(n) differences 3n+1 and 3n+4, gcd restrictions gcd(a,b)|2, gcd(b,c)|2, gcd(a,c)|35 via explicit modular reductions and parity. For n>=6, c<2a makes all three generators minimal. Applied the iff three-generator gluing criterion to every possible nontrivial gcd pair: adjacent pairs excluded by normalized-sum intervals and n=7 check; endpoints d in {5,7,35} excluded by forced x+y=d and nonintegral y=d(3n+1)/(6n+5) after explicit thresholds; remaining n=10,12 fail membership and n=40 succeeds, with n=2..5 direct. Independent Apéry shortest-path vs gluing calculations checked n=2..90 and the four exact F,g values. Finite calculation corroborates only, not universal exclusion.

value.rationale: Symmetry and Gorenstein character of naturally indexed three-generator numerical semigroups is motivated by the published pentagonal Frobenius table. Exactly four survivors, including the large isolated n=40 three-generator gluing, and a uniform finite exclusion argument form a meaningful complete classification, not merely table recomputation.

final_claim: For ordinary pentagonal P(n)=n(3n-1)/2 and every integer n>=2, S_n=<P(n),P(n+1),P(n+2)> is symmetric iff n is one of 2,3,5,40; the Frobenius/genus exceptional pairs are (43,22),(133,67),(1699,850),(258529,129265).
limitations: Ordinary (not centered) pentagonal numbers, three consecutive indices n>=2 only; no general Frobenius/genus formula for all n.
